newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas mixed late, fronts still off.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas mixed late, fronts still off.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were mixed late Tuesday in typically-quiet post-expiration trade, with front months down but holding recent ranges amid little reason to move far in either direction, sources said.
At 1420 EST, March eased two cents to $2.595 per million British thermal units, while April was 1.7 cents lower at $2.29. Others were mixed, with some late 1997s up slightly.

"As long as March stays above $2.46, it doesn't mean a whole lot. For the next week or so, we could just trade in these ranges," said one Houston-based trader, pegging March resistance in the $2.80 area.

Despite revised forecasts calling for colder Midwest and Northeast weather this week, traders said storage, particularly in the East, appeared comfortable, adding March was the start of the weaker-demand shoulder period.
Withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's weekly American Gas Association storage report ranged from 120 to 200 bcf.
Technical traders agreed March support was along the trendline in the $2.50 area and then at the recent $2.46 low. Resistance was seen at $2.70 area and then at $2.80.

In the cash, January Gulf Coast gas firmed five to 10 cents Tuesday to about the $3 level, with Feb on the same pipes talked in the low-to-mid $2.90s. Jan Midcon gained a similar amount to about $3 on colder weather in the region, with Feb quoted in the $2.80 area. New York city gate gas for Januray or February was pegged in the $3.60s.
NYMEX said 16,314 Hub contracts traded by 1350 EST.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1200 EST. February Alberta and Permian natgas expire Wednesday.
On the KCBT, February edged up 0.3 cent to $2.61, while March was still one cent lower at $2.34. The March East/West spread narrowed by one cent to 25.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
KCBT February natgas expires later today.
